warrior.tagline: Heavy iron, short answers, and bad knees in the rain.
warrior.description: A veteran border-guard who treats battlefields like bad weather—something to be endured behind good oak and thick plate. Built to hold choke points, break shield walls, and survive mistakes that would fold lesser mercenaries.
backstory: Twelve years on the Thornwick border taught him two useful habits: check your cinch-straps before dawn, and never volunteer for a parade. He survived three reorganizations of the provincial levy simply by being too stubborn to die and too reliable to dismiss.

When the salt-tax riots turned into full-scale siege warfare, his company was paid in promissory notes stamped by clerks who had already fled south. He kept the shield, pawned the ceremonial sash, and started taking contracts where the silver was weighed upfront.
He does not care who sits on the Obsidian Throne or why the wells went dry. Someone paid to have the road cleared, and he intends to collect before his joints lock up for good.

select: Point me at the thick end.
My shield's ready. My knees aren't.
Keep the silver dry and the orders short.
Let's get this over with before rain.
If it bleeds, I can block it.
hurt: Felt that one in my teeth.
low_hp: Someone bring a bandage—or a shovel.
Not today. Not in this ditch.
Vision's going gray around the edges.
One more hit and I'm done.
level_up: Still learning new ways to hit things.
Good. Now I survive slightly worse odds.
Muscle remembers what the head forgets.
rare_loot: Decent steel. No rust on the tang.
unique_loot: Whoever forged this hated their enemies.
Worth every blister on the march.
idle: Could use a chair and some broth.
victory: Still breathing. Counts as a win.
Patch the shields and move on.
death: Tell Garrick... I want my boots back...
Finally... a place to lie down...

act_reactions.act1_end: Ashbrook's empty, the road south is open, and my boots are already full of dust.
act_reactions.act2_end: All that climbing for a dry cistern. At least the sea breeze smells cleaner.
act_reactions.act3_end: I hate boats. I hate burning boats even more. Point me toward dry rock.
act_reactions.act4_end: The throne's warm, the war's quiet, and nobody's shooting at me. Best contract yet.

npc_asides.line: Add another rivet to the left pauldron, Hobb—cavalry lances keep skidding right into the seam.
Keep your militia behind my shield line, Garrick. Brave boys make messy funerals.
Skip the salted mutton, Bram—give me lamp oil and whetstones before the next ridge.
If this hull leaks twice between Oakhaven and the straits, Kors, I'm swimming back to bill you.
Your vanguard marches too stiff, Rowan. Loose shoulders live longer on volcanic scree.
Now that's a proper anvil, Vok. Keep your tongs off my blade unless you're tempering the edge.

archer.tagline: Good eyes, dry wit, and zero interest in melee.
archer.description: A sharp-tongued reconnaissance hunter who prefers solving problems from sixty paces behind cover. Excels at picking off high-value targets, crippling advancing lines, and reminding heavy infantry how loud they breathe.
backstory: She learned her trade poaching crown deer in the border woods, where getting caught meant losing a thumb and missing a shot meant going hungry. Both lessons stuck remarkably well.

After three winters guiding tax assessors through marshland—and occasionally leaving the rude ones on the wrong side of a peat bog—she discovered that military scouting paid twice as much for half the conversation.
She follows the campaign south mostly out of professional curiosity: someone keeps building bigger walls, and she enjoys finding the drafty gaps in all of them.

select: Let's keep sixty paces between us.
Try not to clank so loud.
hurt: That ruined a perfectly good cloak.
low_hp: I am not built for this!
Patch me up before I faint!
Bad day to forget extra bandages.
rare_loot: Ooh, shiny—and light enough to carry.
Look at the fletching balance on that.
I'll take it before the warrior notices.
unique_loot: Now that's a work of art.
Draws like silk, bites like a viper.
I'm keeping this. Don't even ask.
Worth wading through all that mud.
idle: Do we get paid by the hour?
I could hit that crow from here.
kill_streak: Like shooting barrels in a ditch.
victory: Clean sweep. Salvage the good shafts.
And nobody even mussed my hair.

act_reactions.act1_end: Half a town evacuated and not a single arrow wasted. Honestly, I'm impressed with myself.
act_reactions.act2_end: Turns out the mighty fortress was guarding an empty bucket. Classic management.
act_reactions.act3_end: Setting boats on fire is great for dramatic lighting, terrible for visibility.
act_reactions.act4_end: You actually sat on the flaming chair. Bold choice—I'll stand slightly upwind.

npc_asides.line: Keep the oar steady, Fenwick—hard to line up a clean shot when your boat wobbles like a drunk duck.
Two coppers for a thimble of warm water, Tull? I'd rather lick dew off a cactus.
Your coastal scouts walk like badgers in dry leaves, Lyra. Send them to me for a week.
Keep your pockets out of my quiver, Pip—those broadheads bite harder than harbor crabs.
Just a dab of salve on the forearm, Sera. String-slap is embarrassing enough without a sling.
You carry enough iron chains to sink a skiff, Elias. Ever tried traveling light?

mage.tagline: Precise equations, volatile gestures, and mild dread.
mage.description: A methodical arcana-scholar who views magic not as miracle, but as hazardous thermodynamics. Capable of unraveling formations from afar, provided nothing interrupts the third syllable of the invocation.
backstory: Expelled from the Capital Collegium for publishing a monograph proving that half the state liturgy consisted of corrupted plumbing diagrams, he retreated to the provinces with three trunks of annotated notebooks.
Field work in Thornvael has been deeply inconvenient: rain warps vellum, blood ruins chalk circles, and mercenaries routinely stand inside blast radii despite explicit verbal warnings.
He presses onward toward the Obsidian Core because the ambient ley-drift violates every known conservation law—and leaving an unmeasured anomaly behind would keep him awake for years.

select: Keep your steel clear of my gestures.
Please do not jostle my elbow.
hurt: My robes are not rated for blades!
I am bleeding on my notes!
low_hp: This is a catastrophic margin of error!
level_up: The formula yields cleaner results now.
Ah! That solves the fourth variable.
unique_loot: The ley-lines practically sing through it.
Do not touch the runes with bare hands.
This belongs in a vault—or my pack.
idle: The humidity is ruining my parchment.
Did anyone else hear that hum?
I really should have packed dry socks.
Why is everything here covered in soot?
Silence before a surge. Never good.
victory: A tidy conclusion, all things considered.
Let us record the casualties and leave.

act_reactions.act1_end: Fascinating—Morvessa's hex-seals drew power straight from the border salt-flats. Terrible for agriculture.
act_reactions.act2_end: An entire fortress built atop a dry aquifer. Truly, superstition is the most durable mortar.
act_reactions.act3_end: Combusting pitch on saltwater produces dreadful fumes. My throat may never recover.
act_reactions.act4_end: You bypassed the Anchor Seals entirely. Unorthodox, terrifying, and—I admit—structurally elegant.

npc_asides.line: Your tinctures are remarkably stable, Marta, though your labeling system gives me palpitations.
Those Redmarsh hydraulic glyphs match pre-imperial border markers, Zahra. Let me copy your rubbings.
Fascinating poultice, Sera—mildly antiseptic, though the willow-bark ratio could be refined.
Volcanic slag conducts ember-charge at triple rate, Vok. Wear insulated gloves when quenching.
Your liturgy describes the Anchor Seals as moral weights, Elias. Mechanically, they are pressure valves.
No, Hobb, you cannot hammer rune-silver cold—it fractures along the crystalline grain.
